stories.title: Navi Pillay Awarded Nobel Peace Prize for Contributions to International Justice
stories.summary: Navi Pillay, a South African-born jurist and former UN human rights chief, has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her significant contributions to international law and justice. The Nobel Committee recognized her efforts in promoting peace and her role in addressing war crimes, including her leadership of a UN commission that found Israel guilty of genocide in Gaza. Pillay expressed her initial disbelief upon receiving the news and dedicated the award to survivors of international crimes.

story_report.summary: South African-born jurist Navanethem “Navi” Pillay has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for efforts to promote peace and international law, including advancing prosecution of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. Pillay, who dedicated the award to survivors of international crimes, will join the Nobel Peace Prize’s customary Oslo program, culminating in the Dec. 10 presentation of the medal and diploma and a Nobel lecture. The committee described accountability and the rule of law as essential to lasting peace.
